patch_description:
The program returned an empty list of column orderings and returned a DataFrame whose rows were sorted lexicographically as tuples — it permuted cell values across rows rather than applying per-row column permutations, and it never produced valid per-row column orderings consistent with the returned data (required output). The original code also had fragile attribute-based row handling (`hasattr`/`getattr` on itertuples rows), duplicated values via `result_df.update(group)`, and stripped/rebuilt columns in ways that altered data.

The fix replaces the whole editable block with a simpler, correct algorithm:
- Serialize each cell to string once (missing -> ""), keep the original values.
- Build 2-3 cheap candidate global column orders (frequency-ranked, length-weighted repetition-ranked, and a conditional partition tree that groups rows by a chosen field value and orders suffixes per group).
- Score each candidate by computing the exact serial-Trie character reuse = sum of LCPs of lexicographically adjacent serialized row strings (binary-search LCP on string slices, all C-speed).
- Apply the best per-row column permutation to build the output DataFrame (object dtype, all original values preserved, same shape, no row sorting/merging).
- Return (reordered_df, per-row column orderings lists) consistent with the returned data.

All public method signatures preserved; data and shape fully preserved; handles missing values and mixed types.
